title: Ethiopian Berbere Chicken
community: Modern Ethiopian restaurants — the dry-spiced berbere chicken
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Berbere Chicken — chicken pieces marinated in a berbere, kibbeh, garlic, and ginger paste for 2 hours, then pan-fried or grilled until the berbere crust caramelises magnificently. The dry-spiced berbere chicken — the Ethiopian equivalent of Southern fried chicken, entirely its own creation.
longDesc: Berbere Chicken is what modern Ethiopian restaurants serve when they want to present the berbere tradition in an accessible format — the chicken is marinated, then cooked by high heat rather than slow simmering. The result is a berbere-crusted chicken of extraordinary fragrance and flavour.
ingredients: 8 chicken pieces — bone-in thighs and drumsticks
steps: Mix marinade. Score chicken pieces deeply.
Push marinade into score marks and all over.
Bring to room temperature 30 minutes before cooking.
Pan-fry in a little kibbeh over medium heat: 8—10 minutes per side.
Or grill over charcoal: 10—12 minutes per side.
chefTips: Score the chicken deeply — the berbere must reach the bone.
Medium heat — berbere burns at high heat.
cookingScience: See ETH064 for berbere crust science. In pan-frying, the Maillard reactions and sugar caramelisation of the berbere occur in direct contact with the hot pan surface — producing a crispier, more caramelised crust than oven roasting.
sustainabilityTips: Bone-in chicken pieces — maximum flavour from less premium cuts.
healthBenefits: Less added fat than fried chicken in oil.
culturalNote: Berbere Chicken is Ethiopian food's accessible international ambassador — a format that anyone familiar with spiced chicken can recognise, but flavoured with the most distinctively Ethiopian spice blend in the world.
